steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
Combine flour, oil, milk, sugar, and salt in a 9-inch pie pan; stir with a fork until mixture comes together.
Pat into the bottom and up the sides of the pan.
Poke holes in the bottom and sides with a fork.
Bake in the preheated oven until light golden brown, about 15 minutes. Use as directed in your favorite pie recipe.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Pie Crust
raw_recipe.description: This easy pie crust is so simple to make with flour, sugar, salt, oil, and milk. And best of all, you don't need a mixing bowl or rolling pin!

review.reviewBody: I would not use this recipe (as stated) for desserts. The crust would be too salty for a dessert. However, it would be great for a quiche. If you decrease the salt by half and use a generous tablespoon of sugar (instead of only 2 tsp) - this is great! Fortunately I tasted the dough before pressing it into the pan - and added enough extra sugar to still use it for my pecan pie. Came out fantastic! Since pecan pies typically bake for a long time, I didn't bother baking the crust and it came out cooked through after an hour and a half baking. Rating four stars because this produced a very simple and quick alternative to rolling out a pie crust - and if enough sugar is added, is very tasty!

I have avoided making pie crusts for many years because I could never get it right. They were too much effort and always turned out tough. But I gave this recipe a try and I am absolutely ecstatic to have found such an easy recipe that turned out so well! It was tender, flaky and flavorful! My crust was for a quiche and I used olive oil as another reviewer here suggested. It turned out fantastic. This is a keeper for sure and I am saying goodbye to Pillsbury crusts! Thank you so much for a great recipe that will definitely save me time and money in the kitchen.

An update on my original review - I healthied this recipe up a bit by using 1/2 cup of whole wheat flour plus 1 cup of white flour and it turned out great.

Great recipe, one thing I liked better is substituting Cocoanut milk and then reducing the salt to half teaspoon and reducing the sugar to one teaspoon. Bake ahead of filling with fruit for ten minutes. After filling with fruit or quiche recipe, bake again as suggested. Worked great for my strawberry/apple pie! Thanks.

I knew the moment after viewing the ingredients, I had to tweak in order to use it... Plus, nothing worse than an oily pie crust! It makes a shortbread style crust when patted down thick enough (inorder to avoid cracking). Used it so far for open-faced candied yam cream pie and pulled BBQ pork pie 👍Ingredients (tweaked)-----------------1 1/2 cup all purpose flour, 1 stick unsalted butter (melted), 1 tbsp milk, 1 1/2 tbsp sugar (3 tbsp sugar- dessert pie), * Optional:Pinch of salt to taste(Up to 1/2 tsp)-----------------The directions actually weren't bad at all. Only difference is I use a bowl instead to mix.

I was pleasantly surprised w this crust!! The dough looks oily but it bakes up nicely, flakey and tender. I've used it twice- as written- for quiche. No need to prebake. It held up well in the fridge for a few days- no soggy. Today I used this for a pudding pie. As recommended I used 3T sugar and 1/2 the salt, also added a splash of vanilla, an yes, I baked this one 13 min. Tastes like shortbread.

This was an easy recipe to make...I mixed it all in my kitchen aide and put in the pie plate and spread out then. I added half the salt and a bit more sugar to the recipe. I did use organic raw sugar, unbleached flour and olive oil instead. My family loved the crust with our chocolate pie...it was flaky but held together nicely!! Will make again.

Wanted to make my husband a banana cream pie but didn’t want to spend a whole lot of time on the crust. I found this, read the reviews and gave it a whirl. I doubled the recipe on everything except the salt so I could have an extra crust. I blended the milk and oil together before putting it into the dry ingredients I had already mixed into a bowl. I used a pastry cutter and it came out awesome, not too salty at all. Glad I doubled the recipe so ready for my coconut cream,????

I used a tin pan, and the mixing made the dough have a metal taste. The bottom was too thick due to poor process. Bottom corner and sides cooked up hard and unchewable. The vegetable oil and salt amounts were too much, and made the pumpkin pie taste like salty oil with hard clumps. Use glass pan, less salt to taste, add some sugar to taste. Flour type make a big difference in crusts. Use pastry flour 00 and traditional crust technique.
I used BEEF TALLOW and butter melted. It works fine! Great easy recipe. Mixed in a bowl first and baked at 350 for 5 minutes and 400 for 5 minutes. Came out great. I stink at pie crust!

I was making a wild blackberry pie and took into account previous reviewers' remarks. I decreased the salt to a pinch and used 1 Tablespoon sugar. The pie was phenomenal! This recipe is a keeper. 
P.S.forgot to mention that I also substituted whole wheat pastry flour for the white flour.

Thank you for sharing this awesome and super- easy recipe! I've made two flawless fruit (cherry & blackberry) pies with perfect crumble. I double the recipe, add twice the amount of sugar, divide it for the bottom crust, then add either a touch more sugar or cinnamon for the crumble. The topping turns out crisp and beautifully brown. I've had no issue with the bottom being soggy, even without egg wash. I do think pre-baking the crust is key. A keeper!!

I will change it to a little less salt - 1/4 to 1/2 tsp salt instead of 1 tsp. Also, alert - it is meant to be only one crust and you do not roll out anything. I used 3/4 for the crust and the remaining as crumble on top of my cherry pie. Wonderful!

We have an elderly neighbor who is convalescing after a fall and I wanted to make him his favorite pie (pumpkin). I like this recipe because it's for one crust, I had all the ingredients on hand and it could be done right in the pie plate - no taking out the rolling pin, mat, etc. I found that if I put pieces of crust on the rim first then worked them down the plate to the crust at the bottom, it worked alot better and more uniform than working from the bottom up to the edges. It made a great crust with very little effort. I will be using this again!
Easy to use and very flaky and delicious
There is no need to make any changes… This piecrust is simple and simply wonderful
No perfect just the way it is
